_what: The flat leaper counts at n = 15, read from the OEIS BEFORE this session's own n = 15 enumeration returned anything. They are the external key on the new column: four values by four authors that this project did not compute and could not have known, at the very n in question.
_why_the_order_matters: The same key was used for the n = 14 column on 2026-08-17, and it is the strongest single check in this directory because it certifies the NEW row rather than the old ones. Fetching it after the fact would still be a check, but it would not be a blind one. This file is committed before the flat n = 15 jobs have returned; the git history is the receipt.
offsets_checked: A137774 has offset 1; A189358, A189565 and A189563 have offset 0 and publish a(0) = 1, which moves their term one place along the printed list without moving its index. All four therefore align as our n = a(n). Verified here by reading a(14) back out and matching the committed n = 14 column exactly.

n14_readback._note: these four match terms-1-14.tsv's flat row exactly, which is how the offset alignment is confirmed rather than assumed

n16_for_later._note: recorded only so a future run does not have to re-fetch. n = 16 is roughly thirteen times the cost of n = 15 and is not attempted here.
